title: The Voice That Breathed o’er Eden
description: The Voice That Breathed o’er Eden in Tonic Solfa to BLAIRGOWRIE: the solfa with the words, staff notation, the four verses, and a piano.
about: John Keble wrote the words, first published in the Salisbury Hymn Book in 1857. John Bacchus Dykes wrote the tune BLAIRGOWRIE.
underlay: The voice that breathed o’er E-den, That ear-liest wed-ding day, The pri-mal mar-riage bless-ing, It hath not passed a-way. Still in the pure es-pous-al Of Chris-tian man and maid, The ho-ly Three are with us, The three-fold grace_ is__ said,

lines: The voice that breathed o’er Eden,
The holy Three are with us,
For love and faith’s sweet sake,
Which naught on earth may break.
As Eve Thou gav’st to Adam
Out of his own pierced side:
As Thou didst bind two natures
To bless them as they kneel,
As Thou, for Christ the Bridegroom,
O spread Thy pure wing o’er them,
Let no ill power find place,
To cast their crowns before Thee
Till to the home of gladness
With Christ’s own Bride they rise.
